title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
summary: Join the nodes from two sorted singly linked lists into one sorted list.

contractDetails.constraints: There are 0–50 nodes across the two acyclic input lists. Each value is an integer in [−100, 100]. Both lists are nondecreasing and the inputs do not share nodes. Equal values retain their multiplicity.

statement: Join the nodes from two sorted singly linked lists into one sorted list. Splice the supplied nodes together and return the new head. The judge uses arrays to show each list's values in traversal order.

examples.explanation: The two copies of 2 both appear.
The second list supplies the whole output.
All nodes of the second list come first.

constraints: There are 0–50 nodes across the two acyclic input lists. Each value is an integer in [−100, 100]. Both lists are nondecreasing and the inputs do not share nodes. Equal values retain their multiplicity.
hints: Conceptual: The smaller of the two head values can go next.
Directional: Keep a cursor for each input and a tail for the result.
Implementation: Attach the smaller current node and advance that input. Once one input is exhausted, link the result to the remaining chain.
complexityAnalysis: O(n+m) time and O(1) auxiliary space for input lengths n and m. A dummy head can simplify the first attachment.
